key_insight: MoTok introduces a diffusion-based discrete motion tokenizer within a three-stage Perception–Planning–Control pipeline, enabling planners to use discrete semantic tokens while a diffusion synthesizer preserves high-fidelity kinematics. This bridges the semantic strength of token-based methods and the fine-grained control of continuous diffusion models.
problem_solved: Previous motion-generation approaches either provide strong kinematic fidelity (continuous diffusion) or good semantic conditioning (discrete tokens), but not both. The paper solves how to decouple and connect semantic planning and kinematic control so models can accept semantic conditions without sacrificing motion quality.
method: Perception: extract condition features (semantic labels, language, or scene/context) as inputs for planning.
Planning: generate discrete motion tokens with MoTok — a diffusion-based tokenizer that encodes semantic intent into discrete token sequences.
Control: use a diffusion-based motion synthesizer conditioned on the discrete tokens to reconstruct smooth, high-fidelity kinematic motion.
impact: Allows practitioners to combine interpretable, discrete semantic planning with state-of-the-art continuous motion synthesis, improving controllability and realism for animation, avatars, and robotics. It streamlines pipelines where high-level intent must be translated into physically plausible motion.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Perception → Planning (MoTok tokenizer) → Control (diffusion synthesizer) with dataflow arrows and short annotations.
Comparison chart: discrete-token methods vs continuous-diffusion methods showing trade-offs (semantic control vs kinematic fidelity) and how MoTok combines both.
Token-to-motion illustration: discrete token timeline mapped onto a skeleton animation sequence to show how tokens correspond to motion segments.
Qualitative before/after panels: example motions generated by token-only, diffusion-only, and the combined MoTok pipeline for direct visual comparison.
paper_title: Bridging Semantic and Kinematic Conditions with Diffusion-based Discrete Motion Tokenizer
paper_authors: Chenyang Gu, Mingyuan Zhang, Haozhe Xie, Zhongang Cai, Lei Yang
